summary: A root alias of an unsupported value loses its unknown contribution when joined with a known target
evidence: The root plain-alias arm at lines 126-135 copies the source cell without marking an untracked source unknown. For `let f (x:int)=x; let opaque=(fun k -> k) f; let a=opaque; let choice=if flag then f else a; let run x=choice x`, `opaque` is unsupported and unenrolled, so `a` copies an unseeded bottom cell and `choice` joins `{f}` with bottom. An isolated OCaml 5.3 CMT compiled successfully and the real arch_callgraph_ocaml producer emitted for `run` exactly one `MAY_ENUMERATED f` row with NULL TOP fields and no `MAY_TOP`; the pure-known control `pure_choice=if flag then f else pure_a` produced the identical row. In the same fixture, direct `a x` emitted `MAY_TOP callback_param`, proving the source is unknown at invocation but that uncertainty is lost specifically through the mixed join. This violates specs/ocaml-cfa-foundation.md:166 (FR-005), :183 (FR-019), and the independent-frontier requirements FR-034/FR-036.
fix: When enrolling a root plain alias, preserve an explicit callback_param reason if its resolved source binder is not itself an eligible tracked root value; do not leave that source cell as semantic bottom. Add an authentic CMT regression containing the mixed unsupported-alias/known branch and a pure-known control, asserting that mixed `run` has bounded `f` plus exactly one callback_param unknown while the pure control has bounded `f` only; retain a direct `a x` assertion as the premise control.
boundary: Root single-variable alias enrollment and branch-result CFA joins
invariant: Known targets and unsupported-value uncertainty must propagate independently through aliases and joins.
failure_mode: A mixed known/unknown function value is reported as a closed finite target set, permitting downstream absence queries to treat an open callback frontier as bounded.
